chunks: Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us from Yasir, he said:
When al-Rida (peace be upon him) became the crown prince, I heard him while he had raised his hands toward the sky and said:
O Allah! Surely You know that I am compelled and under necessity,
so do not hold me accountable, just as You did not hold Your servant and prophet Yusuf accountable when he was led into the governance of Egypt.

key_terms.الْعَهْد: The covenant/position — here referring to wilayat al-'ahd (crown prince designation)
key_terms.مُضْطَرٌّ: Under necessity/distress — one left with no alternative option
key_terms.مُكْرَهٌ: Compelled, coerced — one who acts against their will under external pressure
key_terms.وِلَايَة: Governance, authority, rulership over a territory or people

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Rida willingly accept the crown prince position from al-Ma'mun?
ai.summary: Yasir, a servant and companion of Imam al-Rida (AS), narrates a deeply personal moment: when Caliph al-Ma'mun forced the Imam to accept the role of crown prince in 201 AH, the Imam immediately raised his hands in supplication, declaring to God that he accepted this position under compulsion, not by choice. He drew a parallel to Prophet Yusuf (AS), who was similarly thrust into political authority in Egypt without seeking it. This hadith is pivotal in Shia tradition as evidence that the Imam's acceptance of the crown prince position was coerced, preserving his political innocence.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. `Ali b. Ibrahim (rh) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Yasir.
He said: When al-Rida (as) became the crown prince, he raised his hands to the sky and I heard him say:
O Allah! Surely, You know that I dislike and despair this.
So, do not hold me accountable, just as You did not hold Your servant and prophet Yusuf accountable when he came into power in Egypt.
